messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] vectorizing transforms
parts:
On 6/24/13 11:04 AM, Peter Li wrote:
> I don't think I understand what you're saying completely. So for the new vari type, is it supposed to just take in the
> jacobian matrix and compute the determinant?

However you have to implement it, there should be a single
vari for the log Jacobian determinant that gets added to the
log probability parameter being passed in.

The point is to make the entire transform stage of Stan faster.

For example, suppose we have:

parameters {
real<lower=L> x[N];
...
}

The transform to constrained space is

x[n] |--> exp(x[n]) + L

So the Jacobian is diagonal so the log determinant is
just sum(x). So you won't even need a new type in
this case.

The lower-bound L may be a variable, but even if it is,
dL/dx = 0 because the bound L can't depend on x because
of variable declaration ordering constraints in Stan (can't
use a variable before it's fully declared).

So why don't you start with this case.

The full set of transforms we use and their Jacobian determinants
are defined in the manual.
> Also, should I separate the transforms into their own files (i.e. refactor like we did for agrad/fvar/math)?

I understand how the jacobian plays into this, but I'm still confused
about defining a vari for it and how to use it. Right now, I have
something like

template <typename T, typename TL>
inline
typename return_type<T,TL>::type>::type
lb_constrain(const T& x, const TL& lb, T& lp) {

if (!(stan::length(x)))
return 0.0;

double res(0.0);

agrad::OperandsAndPartials<T> operands_and_partials(x);
VectorView<const T> x_vec(x);
size_t N = max_size(x);
for (size_t n = 0; n < N; n++) {
const double x_dbl = value_of(x_vec[n]);

lp += x_dbl;

res += exp(x_dbl) + lb;

if (!is_constant_struct<T>::value)
operands_and_partials.d_x1[n] += exp(x_dbl);
}

return operands_and_partials.to_var(res);
}

But I'm not sure how I should be treating res--should it be a vector at
least type T to match x?


Peter

parts:
Now I see the issue.

The model:

parameters {
real<lower=0> y[10];
}
model {
y ~ normal(0,1);
}

translates the constraints to:

vector<T__> y;
size_t dim_y_0__ = 10;
y.reserve(dim_y_0__);
for (size_t k_0__ = 0; k_0__ < dim_y_0__; ++k_0__) {
y.push_back(in__.scalar_lb_constrain(0,lp__));
}

So in order to do what I want, we need to change the generated
code to something like:

vector<T__> y = in__.scalar_lb_constrain_array(dim_y_0__,0,lp__);

Then scalar_lb_constrain_array() would generate a single vari
instance to add to lp__ for the Jacobian.

So either you're going to have to dive into the generator code
in stan/gm, or wait until I get to it.

- Bob
